title: Adaptive hybrid preheat for tenant prioritization and KV coalescing
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Problem: Dedicated fleets still observe tail latency spikes and token-cost variability from cold-starts when tenants burst or after model swaps. Existing warm pool and KV-seed approaches are static: they either over-provision memory for many tenants or under-prepare high-priority tenants, and they do not consolidate KV priming across similar request prefixes.

Goal: Build an adaptive hybrid preheat controller that combines tenant-priority scoring, time-decayed demand forecasts, and in-flight KV coalescing to allocate warm pool budget and trigger targeted weight streaming and KV priming. The controller should guarantee throughput SLOs for high-priority tenants while reducing overall warm-resident memory by coalescing overlapping KV prefixes and opportunistically using ephemeral weight residency.

Approach:
1) Tenant prioritization: compute a dynamic priority score per tenant from SLA tier, recent QPS, percentile latency breaches, and contract throughput guarantees.
2) Hybrid preheat modes: fast-path preheat (small subset of weights + KV top-50 keys) for bursty tenants; deep preheat (full model residency) for sustained high-throughput tenants.
3) KV coalescing: maintain a rolling aggregator that merges top-k prefixes across concurrent warm requests and schedules a single priming job instead of multiple similar jobs.
4) Budget allocation: global warm-pool budget respected; controller uses priority-weighted allocation and preemptible ephemeral reservoirs for opportunistic prefetching.
5) Autoscale integration: signals exposed to autoscaler to provision extra nodes when predicted aggregate warm demand exceeds threshold; fallback policy to lower-fidelity quantized variants when capacity unavailable.

Trade-offs considered: aggressive deep preheat lowers cold-starts but increases memory pressure and costs; coalescing reduces duplicate priming work but adds latency to the first request if aggregation window is too long. We propose conservative aggregation windows (50-200ms) and a per-tenant max cold-sla that enforces deep preheat when breached repeatedly.
acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate 90th percentile request latency reduction of >=35% for priority tenants on synthetic burst tests compared to baseline warm-pool
Reduce duplicate KV priming jobs by >=60% as measured by priming-job counts per minute in the dedicated fleet
Maintain global warm-pool memory usage within configured budget (±5%) while meeting throughput SLO for P1 tenants during 1-hour synthetic ramp tests
Integration tests that verify autoscaler receives predicted demand pulses and scales within configured cooldown windows
Operational runbook and console dashboard panels for preheat activity, per-tenant priority, and priming job traces

experiments: A/B: baseline warm-pool vs hybrid preheat on a 10-tenant testbed (3 high-priority, 7 best-effort)
KV coalescing window sweep: 25ms, 50ms, 100ms, 200ms — measure p50/p90 and duplicate priming rate
Budget allocation policy variants: strict cap vs. elastic preemptible reservoir — compare cost and SLA violations
